title: Lens: standards enforcement and tooling
summary: Where tools run, they are strict and unusually well engineered. services/agent has ruff, ruff format, strict mypy and strict pytest. apps/web has strict TypeScript (with noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes), zero-warning ESLint, Prettier and a production build. Every check runs offline, cannot change the tree, counts skips and empty suites as failures, and is proven by known-bad fixtures. Enforcement stops at directory boundaries rather than where the rules intend. The 133 repository-level Python files (25,788 lines, 42% of all Python, including the verifier, the hooks, the qualifiers and the persistent install) have no lint, format or type gate. They follow a second house style and carry 295 dead suppressions, and the 881 service names they import are checked only when a slow profile runs them. packages/api-client's runtime and contract test, and the infra JavaScript, fall outside lint and format. Tests are selected from hand-kept lists, so schema-value.test.ts and the static manifest suite run in no profile. Nothing documents the five test mechanisms or why the web unit runner departs from DH-06. Neither language sets size or complexity limits. No rule stops the 28 type assertions on response bodies, most of which skip an available generated parser. Layering is clean but unguarded, and one web import cycle exists. Nothing runs any profile automatically, and no test guards the gates' own settings. Most fixes are configuration with zero or small baselines. Ruff's RUF100 and ESLint's bulk suppressions make those baselines shrink-only.

scores.why: Strict, pinned, fault-proven gates cover services/agent and apps/web. 42% of Python (133 files) and the infra JS run under none, packages/api-client is type-checked but not linted or format-checked, nothing triggers the gates, and their settings are unguarded.

Web layering and domain/ are clean today (0 hits under the proposed zones and bans). One web import cycle exists, adapters and application import each other (26 and 21 statements), and no rule holds any direction.
No limit is configured. 33 service functions exceed lenient thresholds (41 hits), web functions reach 677 lines and files 829 counted lines, and a script holds a 410-line function.
62 service functions take more than five parameters (8 take more than eight). Pure helpers such as valueFor and draftOf live inside component files, out of unit-test reach.
Directory boundaries, not intent, decide coverage. Tests span five mechanisms in six places, and packages/api-client falls between the web's lint and format paths.
The verification design is a model: offline, pinned, non-mutating, fingerprinted, skip-is-failure and fault-proven. Hand-kept test lists and the lack of any automatic trigger undercut it.
Service suppressions carry codes and reasons. 295 noqa comments in tests/db and scripts are unused, and 25 type: ignore comments target a type checker that never runs.

Strict mypy and strict TypeScript where applied. No rule stops 28 type assertions on response bodies and 2 on JSON.parse, type-aware lint is off, and 881 service names imported by checks and scripts go unchecked statically.

Tooling shares one 0/1/2 exit contract and never passes a timeout or missing tool. Nothing lints the service's 22 broad catches (BLE001), and verify.run_check leaves descendant processes alive on timeout.

Skip-as-failure and known-bad fixtures are exemplary. Selection is hand-kept (one unit test and a static suite run in no profile), the five runners are undocumented, and component logic has no unit-test path.
Strong gates cover about half the code. The rest, the gates' settings and the triggers are unguarded, and most fixes are configuration with small, shrink-only baselines.

strengths.title: Verification cannot install or mutate, and proves it
strengths.evidence: scripts/toolchain.py:187-188 sets UV_OFFLINE, UV_NO_SYNC and COREPACK_ENABLE_NETWORK=0 for checks. run_guarded (scripts/toolchain.py:299-321) fails a run whose locks, manifests, changed files or installed package names differ, even when every step passed. scripts/verify.py:184-187 records the same guard as non_mutation_guard. Use this as the template for every new step.

strengths.title: Skips, empty suites, timeouts and missing tools never pass
strengths.evidence: scripts/verify.py:91-107 turns an empty unittest suite or any skip into a failure and reads pytest's skip summary. scripts/harness_lib.py:221-229 refuses reports with skipped tests or failed commands. verify.py, toolchain.py and qualify_faults.py share one exit contract: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 unavailable.

strengths.title: Known-bad fixtures prove each checker bites
strengths.evidence: scripts/qualify_faults.py:55-75 runs ruff, mypy, pytest, tsc and ESLint on good and bad fixtures. A bad fixture counts only if it fails with its expected marker (F401, return-value, TS2322, no-explicit-any), so a crashed tool is not a detected fault. Add a bad fixture with every new rule.

strengths.title: Strict typing where it is applied
strengths.evidence: services/agent/pyproject.toml:49-59 sets mypy strict over src and tests, pytest --strict-markers --strict-config and strict asyncio mode. All 62 service type: ignore comments carry an error code. apps/web/tsconfig.json:7-9 adds noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes to strict, and apps/web/package.json:6 fails lint on any warning.

strengths.title: Repository conventions as small stdlib tests that check themselves
strengths.evidence: tests/toolchain/test_scaffold_scope.py:41-50 bans the unused provider SDKs and proves each import form is detected. tests/harness/test_shared_form_controls.py:14-23 bans raw form controls and fails if it no longer sees more than 20 screens. Reuse this shape for test ownership and import contracts.

strengths.title: Generated validators and server-only guards at the web boundary
strengths.evidence: 25 component files use generated parse functions at 60 sites, e.g. apps/web/components/approvals-panel.tsx:143. Five server modules begin with import "server-only" (apps/web/lib/bff.ts:1). All 237 internal imports in app, components and lib use the @/ alias, with none relative, which makes path-based layering rules easy to write.

strengths.title: Exact, hashed pins, refused when inexact
strengths.evidence: scripts/toolchain.py:109-121 refuses any pin that is not an exact version, and a pnpm packageManager without its sha512. pnpm-workspace.yaml sets engineStrict, strictPeerDependencies and verifyDepsBeforeRun: error.

strengths.title: Habits that already meet lockable rules
strengths.evidence: DTZ, S602, S604 and S605 report 0 across all 318 Python files, and so do S110 and S112. The web reports 0 floating or misused promises (rerun with type information over 95 files) and 0 layering violations under the proposed zones. These rules can start as errors with no baseline.

findings.title: Repository-level Python runs under no lint, format or type gate

locations.note: ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy run from services/agent with no path arguments
Ruff run without paths checks the services/agent directory, and mypy's files are src and tests
tests/harness and .claude/hooks fall to the harness domain, which runs no static check
the edit-time ruff diagnostic runs only for the python domain
F401: other_resources imported and unused, one of 5,775 hits
F841: workspace_b assigned and never used

findings.evidence: toolchain.py:210-213 runs `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` from services/agent with no paths, and pyproject.toml:52 sets mypy `files = ["src", "tests"]`. Whatever domain check_domains gives a script, the Python steps lint only services/agent. tests/harness and .claude/hooks map to the harness domain, which runs only unittest. The PostToolUse hook runs ruff only for the python domain. So 133 files and 25,788 lines (42% of all Python) have no static check. They include verify.py, harness_lib.py, dispatch.py, the qualifiers and persistent_install.py. Under the service's own rules (metrics.md section 6) they give 5,775 hits: 5,269 E501, 295 RUF100, 119 I001, 34 UP017, 9 B023, 7 F401, 7 RUF012, 7 RUF059, 4 B905, 3 ASYNC240 and 2 F841. 458 of them have safe autofixes.
findings.impact: DH-06 asks for Ruff and strict mypy on owned modules, and DH-09 treats check infrastructure as the most conservative scope. Yet the code that decides whether every other check passed, and the guarded persistent install, has no static check. Its defects surface as wrong verdicts or as runtime failures on the real install. The unused workspace_b at qualify_backup.py:89, a second owner's workspace that nothing reads, may already mark a check the backup qualifier never makes.
findings.recommendation:
Create one shared Python standard. Add a root ruff.toml and have services/agent extend it. Add a repo_ruff_check step over scripts, tests and .claude/hooks to fast and full, and a check_domains domain for those paths so fast, the Stop hook and the PostToolUse diagnostic cover them. Adoption path:
1. Report only, with `ruff check --exit-zero --statistics`.
2. One explicit commit applying the 458 safe fixes and `--select RUF100 --fix`, after the rule selection is settled (XTOL-14).
3. Gate with E501 ignored for these paths.
4. Reformat separately (XTOL-04).
5. Drop the E501 ignore.

Land the import-contract check (XTOL-03) before considering mypy there.
findings.sketch:
# ruff.toml (repository root): the shared Python standard
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
src = ["scripts", "services/agent/src"]
extend-exclude = ["tests/faults/python/bad_*"]   # deliberately bad fixtures
[lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "ASYNC", "RUF"]
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"scripts/**" = ["E501"]          # until the one-time reformat
"tests/**" = ["E501"]
".claude/hooks/**" = ["E501"]

# services/agent/pyproject.toml: inherit instead of restating; no own select
[tool.ruff]
extend = "../../ruff.toml"
src = ["src", "tests"]

# scripts/toolchain.py check_steps, run from the root
Step('repo_ruff_check', (str(venv_bin / 'ruff'), 'check', 'scripts', 'tests', '.claude/hooks'), root)
# scripts/harness_lib.py: a domain that fast and the Stop hook require
REPO_PYTHON_STEPS = frozenset({'repo_ruff_check'})
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 (Ruff lint and format, mypy strict for owned modules; safe autofix is an explicit operation) and DH-05 (substantive checks live in repository scripts; no formatter rewrites in hooks). The change only adds checks, and the hook stays diagnostic.
findings.verifierNote: 133 files and 25,788 lines recounted from files.txt (42% of 61,654 Python lines), and both cited hits reproduce; the 9 B023 hits look benign. Revised: the RUF100 cleanup waits until the rule selection is settled, so the reasoned BLE001 markers survive (XTOL-14).

findings.title: Hand-kept test lists let tests drop out unseen, and two suites already run in no profile

locations.note: web_unit_tests names two of the three unit test files
US-16.2's test, run by no profile
only test_scaffold_scope.py runs; the comment says the rest bootstrap copies from registries
offline static tests of pins, locks and the runbook, run by no profile
19 of the 28 Playwright name filters, kept inline
three more filters in another script
manual by design, recorded only in a comment

findings.evidence: verify.py:161-162 passes only request-guard.test.ts and credential-precedence.test.ts to `node --test`. schema-value.test.ts, added by US-16.2, is in no list, and .checks/full/latest.json records exactly those two files in web_unit_tests' argv. The archived US-16.2 verification.md cites schema-value.test.ts for a PASS row and says fast passed its 'web unit tests'. test_manifests.py calls itself 'Static tests of pins, locks and the runbook' and makes no network call. toolchain_scope_tests discovers only test_scaffold_scope.py, so no report's check argv names test_manifests.py. Playwright specs are chosen by 28 name filters spread over qualify_identity.py (including its -g runs at 329-376), qualify_web.py, qualify_release.py:342 and persistent_install.py:720. All 41 specs match one today except install.spec.ts, which is manual by design, but nothing would notice a new spec that matches none.
findings.impact: The profiles' skip-is-failure rules cannot see an unrun test, and evidence records can cite one as passing. That has already happened once. A pin changed without its runbook row also goes uncaught.
findings.recommendation: Select tests by glob, not by name: Node 22 expands `--test` patterns itself. Add test_manifests.py to the offline toolchain step. Move the Playwright filters into one module the qualifiers import. Add a stdlib harness test that every test file is claimed by a runner or listed as manual with a reason, plus a self-check that an unclaimed file is detected (the test_shared_form_controls.py pattern).
findings.ruleCheck: DH-09 (no passing badge for an empty suite; skipped checks never count) and the OhMyOrch delivery rule (never report a scenario as passing without observing it). The change adds coverage and a guard and removes no check.
findings.verifierNote: verify.py and the full report argv list two of the three unit files, and test_manifests.py only reads repository files. The archived US-16.2 record cites schema-value.test.ts in PASS rows (verification.md:13, 17) and line 22 says fast passed its web unit tests. Filter coverage simulated with regular expressions.

findings.title: Service internals used by the database checks and scripts are never checked statically

locations.note: a services/agent change affects only the python domain
imports the private _keep_lease
imports the private _finish
returns tuple[object, dict] to keep a lazy import
type: ignore[attr-defined] on Ledger.settle and committed in the paid goal
the signature those calls rely on

findings.evidence:
# scripts/persistent_install.py:288 and 437
def reserve_goal(ledger_path: Path, limit: int) -> tuple[object, dict]:
        ledger.settle(entry, 0, 'not_started')  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
A stdlib resolver written for this review checked the 881 names that 68 files in tests/ and scripts/ import from autobots. Those include 473 import lines in 60 tests/db files and 18 imports of 13 private names, such as _keep_lease and _finish. All resolve today, but no tool checks them on change. mypy covers only services/agent, and check_domains sends services/agent/ to the python domain alone. A rename therefore passes fast, the PostToolUse diagnostic and the Stop hook, and breaks only inside the next db run (about 610 s with Docker in the latest report). The 25 type: ignore comments in scripts and tests serve a type checker that never runs there; 14 of them are in persistent_install.py, all caused by reserve_goal's object return type.
findings.impact: A service refactor can silently break the database and qualification suites. It can also break settlement of the shared spending cap after a paid install goal. The failure appears late, in the slowest profile or on the real install.
findings.recommendation: Add an import-contract test to the fast profile, in the style of tests/toolchain/test_scaffold_scope.py. It resolves every `from autobots... import name` in tests/ and scripts/ against services/agent/src. The review's resolver is about 60 lines and runs in under a second. Include a fixture proving a missing name is reported. Type reserve_goal with a TYPE_CHECKING import of Ledger and drop its 14 ignores. Once the lint gate lands, consider mypy with a non-strict override over scripts and tests/db.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 (mypy for owned modules; keep typing exceptions narrow and documented) and python-worker.md (checks use prepared environments and do not install). The check is static and needs no services.
findings.verifierNote: An AST recount gives 881 names in 68 files and 473 statements in 60 tests/db files, and all 14 ignores in persistent_install.py follow from the object type. Revised: the 18 private-name imports cover 13 distinct names.

findings.title: Two Python house styles, and only the service's is checked

locations.note: 100 columns and ruff format defaults (double quotes)
repository scripts use single quotes
a scripts/ file in the service style
a harness test in the service style
a 578-character line

findings.evidence: String literals, counted with tokenize including f-strings: services/agent/src has 7,369 double-quoted and 47 single-quoted; scripts 8,648 single and 978 double; tests/db 9,432 single and 711 double; and tests/harness 2,978 single and 360 double. Nine repository-level files follow the service, among them scripts/specs.py, tests/harness/test_specs.py and tests/db/tool_keys_check.py. Lines over 100 columns: 11 in the service (src and tests, longest 116); 2,060 in scripts (626 over 140, longest 578 at app_db.py:117); 2,763 in tests/db (1,117 over 140). `ruff format --line-length 100` would change 121 of 134 files: 43,508 diff lines, or 34,007 with quote-style preserve. On a scratch copy it grows them from 25,788 to 47,666 lines (41,473 at 120 columns) and leaves 1,015 E501 hits (437 at 120).
findings.impact: Reviewers read two dialects. Very long lines hide logic in diffs. Formatting nearly doubles the true size of this code, which any Python size limit must account for.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the service's style everywhere through the shared root ruff.toml: double quotes, 100 columns. After the lint gate lands, and with no story open on those files, reformat repository-level Python in one mechanical commit listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs. Then add `ruff format --check` for those paths, drop their E501 ignore and wrap the remaining long strings. Calibrate Python size limits after the reformat, and prefer statement and complexity limits to line counts.
findings.sketch:
# ruff.toml (root)
[format]
quote-style = "double"   # the service's style; "preserve" would cut the churn by about 22%

# .git-blame-ignore-revs
<sha>  # one mechanical ruff format of scripts/, tests/ and .claude/hooks/

# scripts/toolchain.py, after the reformat
Step('repo_ruff_format', (str(venv_bin / 'ruff'), 'format', '--check', 'scripts', 'tests', '.claude/hooks'), root)
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 (Ruff check and formatting are separate gates; safe autofix is an explicit operation) and DH-05 (no formatter rewrites on ordinary edits). The reformat is one reviewed commit, never a hook action. It needs harness, db and operations reruns because tests/db and the qualifiers change.
findings.verifierNote: Single-quote and long-line counts reproduce, and the three named files are double-quoted. Revised: the double-quote counts include f-strings here, so they are higher; the format churn comes from the reviewer's scratch copy and was not rerun (metrics.md records 121 of 134 files to reformat).

findings.title: No size or complexity limit is configured in either language

locations.note: lint.select has no C90 or PLR09 rules
Next presets only
--max-warnings=0, so a warn-level rule fails lint
complexity 37, 92 statements
677-line component, complexity 39
527 lines, complexity 37
410-line function

findings.evidence: Counted in this review over the service's src and tests at the proposed thresholds. C901 at 15: 5 (at 12: 17; at 10: 26). PLR0911 at 8 returns: 6. PLR0912 at 15 branches: 2. PLR0913 at 8 arguments: 8 (at 5: 62). PLR0915 at 60 statements: 3. PLR0917 at 6 positional arguments: 17 (at 5: 38). That makes 41 hits on 33 functions in 25 files. Repository-level C901 at 15: scripts 18, tests/db 6, tests/harness 1. Web, non-test: complexity at 15: 11; max-lines-per-function at 150: 24; max-lines at 400: 10, with 6 more in tests/browser.
findings.impact: Hotspots grow without any signal. Because lint fails on any warning, a new limit cannot be introduced at warn level inside the gate.
findings.recommendation: Enable calibrated limits now, with baselines that can only shrink. Ruff: enable the rules, then run `ruff check --add-noqa` once. RUF100, already on through RUF, then fails on any suppression that is no longer needed. ESLint: enable the rules as errors and baseline them with `eslint --suppress-rule`, which writes eslint-suppressions.json and, by default, fails on entries that no longer match. For a report-only look first, use `ruff check --exit-zero --statistics` and a separate `lint:report` script with --max-warnings=-1. As baselines empty, tighten C901 from 15 to 12 to 10 and function length from 150 to 100. Relax file length for tests/browser.
findings.sketch:
# services/agent/pyproject.toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
extend-select = ["C90", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "PLR0917"]
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 15        # 5 today; then 12 (17) and 10 (26)
[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 8               # 8 today
max-positional-args = 6    # 17
max-branches = 15          # 2
max-statements = 60        # 3
max-returns = 8            # 6

// apps/web/eslint.config.mjs
{ files: ["**/*.{ts,tsx}"], rules: {
    complexity: ["error", 15],                                                                    // 11
    "max-lines-per-function": ["error", { max: 150, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }],  // 24
    "max-lines": ["error", { max: 400, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }] } },           // 10
{ files: ["tests/**"], rules: { "max-lines": "off", "max-lines-per-function": "off" } },

# baselines, once each
(cd services/agent && .venv/bin/ruff check --add-noqa)
(cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/eslint --suppress-rule complexity --suppress-rule max-lines-per-function --suppress-rule max-lines .)
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06 (small cohesive modules) and DH-09 (no speculative frameworks or arbitrary quotas). Thresholds are calibrated to today's counts and only tighten; DH-04 forbids raising one to pass a gate.
findings.verifierNote: Every Python count reproduces with ruff 0.17.3, where PLR0917 is stable, and the web counts match eslint_proposed.json. ESLint 9.39.5 has --suppress-rule, and stale suppressions fail unless --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions is set.

findings.evidence: Run in check mode for this review, import/no-cycle reports run-list.tsx:8 and run-panel.tsx:9. import/no-restricted-paths with the three zones below reports 0; an inverted zone reported 59, so the @/ alias resolves. no-restricted-imports patterns for components/ui, components and lib also report 0. findings.evidence: Counted over all 318 Python files in this review. DTZ (naive datetimes): 0. S602, S604 and S605 (shell execution): 0. TID251, banning the unused and non-OpenRouter SDKs: 0. The SDK ban exists only as a test that only the full profile runs, so an edit gets no warning. BLE001 finds 22 broad catches in services/agent/src, 3 in scripts and 2 in .claude/hooks, none annotated. Ruff cannot see log_event, so it also flags handlers that do log: about 10 of the 22 log a named event and 2 raise a new error. The silent ones include `except Exception: return _denied("review_unavailable")`.
findings.impact: Rules a pinned linter checks in milliseconds depend on reviewers noticing, and nothing marks which broad catches are deliberate.
findings.recommendation: Select DTZ, S602, S604, S605 and TID251 in the shared config as errors. They need no baseline and then also run in the PostToolUse diagnostic. Add BLE001 and run `ruff check --add-noqa`, then write the reason on each of the 27 current sites, so each kept broad catch says why and any new one needs a reason. Keep test_scaffold_scope.py.

findings.title: Five test mechanisms, and the web unit runner departs from DH-06 without a decision

locations.note: pytest: services/agent/tests
unittest: tests/harness
node --test: api-client and web unit tests

findings.evidence: Five mechanisms run the tests. pytest runs services/agent/tests. unittest runs tests/harness and tests/toolchain on the standard library, so harness needs no prepared environment. node --test runs the api-client contract test and two of the three web unit files (XTOL-02) through Node type stripping. Playwright runs 40 of the 41 specs through four qualifier scripts; install.spec.ts is run by hand. 44 tests/db *_check.py scripts print JSON cases that app_db.py and the qualifiers relay. DH-06 names Vitest and React Testing Library for pure and client behavior. US-1.3's proposal deferred them to 'the story that first has behavior to test', and later stories used node --test with no decision record. node --test loads only modules with no @/ alias, no server-only import and no JSX. So valueFor and draftOf, pure helpers inside component files, are reachable only through Playwright, as is the decision logic in the onKey handler at approvals-panel.tsx:229 (complexity 27).
findings.impact: Contributors cannot tell where a new test belongs, and the riskiest client logic has no fast test path.
findings.recommendation: Record a short decision naming each mechanism's scope and the reason for it, as DH-09 asks for exceptions. Then either move pure component logic into leaf lib/ modules covered by node --test, or adopt Vitest and React Testing Library in a scoped story with pinned versions. Document the tests/db JSON-case protocol in the harness runbook.

#!/bin/sh
# .githooks/pre-commit. Opt in with: git config core.hooksPath .githooks
# DH-05: the same runner as the assistant hooks; bypassable, so never the completion check.
exec python3.12 scripts/verify.py --profile fast

# Makefile
check:        # harness only, so it works before bootstrap; it already validates the backlog
	python3.12 scripts/verify.py --profile harness
check-fast:   # needs scripts/toolchain.py bootstrap
	python3.12 scripts/verify.py --profile fast

# CI, if adopted: pinned node, python3.12 and uv on PATH
#   -> python3.12 scripts/toolchain.py bootstrap -> python3.12 scripts/verify.py --profile full
findings.ruleCheck: DH-05 (Git hooks may call the same runner; bypassable hooks are not the only completion check) and AGENTS.md (no installs or services in hooks). The hook runs fast only, and the opt-in is explicit, not a silent settings change.
findings.verifierNote: .github is absent, core.hooksPath is unset, .git/hooks holds only samples, and make check validates the backlog twice; durations match the latest reports within a second. Revised: fast needs a prepared toolchain, so the Makefile gains a target instead of repointing check.

findings.title: verify.py keeps a weaker subprocess runner beside toolchain.run_step

locations.note: subprocess.run with a literal 60-second timeout
run_step is already imported
new session, group kill, bounded output
a third copy of the group-kill logic
exit codes and utc() are also defined twice (toolchain.py:48 and :225)

findings.evidence: run_check calls `subprocess.run(argv, ..., timeout=60)`. On timeout CPython kills only the direct child, so processes a test started keep running, whereas toolchain.run_step starts a new session and kills the whole group. The harness suite uses 24 to 27 s of that fixed 60 s in the latest reports. EXIT_* and utc() are defined in both verify.py and toolchain.py.
findings.impact: Two runners in one verifier time out differently. As the harness suite grows, it will hit an unnamed limit and may leave stray processes behind.
findings.recommendation: Move the group-kill process runner into one helper that run_step, run_check and probe_version share, with a named timeout constant for the harness checks, and keep each report's fields (command_argv, duration_seconds). Import the exit codes and utc() from one module.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-05 (deadlines and bounded output for checks). Behavior is unchanged except that a timeout also ends descendants.
findings.verifierNote: The literal 60-second timeout, the two group-kill copies and the duplicated constants confirmed; harness_behavior_tests took 23.7 to 26.2 s. Revised: the reports carry fields run_step does not write, so share the process helper rather than swap the runner.
